newsitem.title: UK: Ldn freight-Capers steady, Atlantic Pamanaxes firm.
newsitem.headline: Ldn freight-Capers steady, Atlantic Pamanaxes firm.

text.p: The London dry cargo freight market ended the week very quietly, still under the influence of holidays in the West and Asia.

Brokers believed that the conditions for Capers worldwide remained fully steady and also continued firm in the Atlantic for Panamaxes. It was said that the rising demand from charterers of clean petroleum products from the US Gulf to the Continent was attracting OBO tonnage which might diminish still further the supply of vessels available for minerals cargoes.
The BFI was down 2 points to 1511.

Periandros of Korinthos 148,011 dwt passing Gibraltar westbound Jan 6 was rumoured fixed for transatlantic grain but further information was lacking, brokers said. Agrotrade fixed Merak S for 20,000/5 tonnes soyabean meal pellets from Sao Francisco do Sul to Rijeka or Koper for Jan 5/10 at $23.50.

Wen Zhou Hai was said to have been fixed by S Korean charterers for 54,000 heavy grain NoPac/Japan for mid-Jan at about $14.00/14.25 no combo but confirmation was not available. Western Bulkcarriers were linked with the T K Bosun-relet Irene 42,260 dwt delivery Singapore for a trip via S Australia with grain to Saudi Arabia at unknown levels. Very little solid news of concluded fixtures surfaced.

Added to an already-firm January Atlantic market were fresh orders from Bunge for up to 5m cft grain Mississippi/Holland for Jan 15/30, Continental 3m cft grain US Gulf/Shanghai for Jan 13/2 (probably workable on timecharter) and 2.5/3m cft US Gulf/E Med including Israel for mid-Jan, and Toepfer with 3.2/4.2m cft grain Mississippi/Lisbon-Hamburg range for Jan 15/24 and 25,000/10 wheat Up River/Tunisia for Jan 18/25.

Reports circulated of Caper period timecharter business. The newbuilding S G Fortune 186,000 dwt was said to have been fixed by Cobam delivery ex-yard S Korea March/April for 3 years at an average of about $16,000 daily plus options of one upon one further years at unknown levels. Some brokers believed this fixture was concluded towards the end of last year. Sea Gloria 157,462 dwt was rumoured fixed for period to Baotrans, following owner's fixture of the sister vessel Sea Grace to Kleimar, but details were not forthcoming.

Interbulk were said to have taken Leopardi 129,088 dwt in the Atlantic for about 6-9 months, believed to be initially for charterer's Richards Bay/Denmark contract with SK Power, but again full details were lacking. Panamax news included reports that Frontline fixed Saldanha Bay/Swinousjie ironore at between $10.00 and 10.25, and Norsk Hydro booked tonnage for about 50,000 phosphate Aqaba/Vlaardingen for mid-Jan at a minimum of $9.00. In the Atlantic Klaveness were said to be working a Panamax for phosphate from Morocco to Pascagoula for loading about Jan 20 at $6.50/7.00.
